proof_summary: Induction through the product recurrence shows that both components at index $n$ are divisible by $2^{n-4}$, while periodicity modulo $5$ and $7$ proves the first component is nonzero (using modulus $5$ when $n\equiv1\pmod3$ and modulus $7$ otherwise). Hence for fixed $k\ge2$, every sufficiently late term has at least $k$ factors of $2$ and is nonzero, so its $k$-th prime factor is $2$ and the sequence is eventually constant.
